name: Review Management
title: Review Management: operator and guest paths and what can go wrong

BANDS.s: Match provider accounts and listings to the restaurant.
Follow submission, collection and stale feed recovery.
Find the right review and choose how to respond.
Check what the guest and operator can see.
Review insights, mobile summaries and connection changes.

NODES.d: Open the restaurant review workspace and inspect the onboarding or overview state.
e: An established restaurant lands back on first use
Old location counts remain after switching restaurants

NODES.d: Authorise Google and select the business location. A connected account also needs a stored location before the first fetch.
e: Operator has access to the account but selects the wrong listing

NODES.d: Select the Yelp business for this restaurant and check the displayed business name. Fetch readiness requires the stored listing.
e: Two similarly named branches are confused
Reviews attributed to the wrong branch
Connected indicator appears before the selected location is saved

NODES.d: Use the Tripadvisor connection flow for the selected restaurant. It can contribute reviews independently of the other sources.
e: Wrong listing is paired with the restaurant
Ratings do not describe this location
Operator expects Tripadvisor to support the Google reply workflow

NODES.d: Fetch requires at least one connected source and all connected sources to be ready. Repair an incomplete connection and try again.
e: One incomplete listing blocks the fetch for other ready sources
Disabled action gives no indication which source needs attention

NODES.d: A guest posts a rating and optional text at the chosen provider. The original review belongs to that provider.
e: Guest posts to a neighbouring branch
Review is missing from the intended inbox
Rating without text is overlooked in a text search

NODES.d: Fetch reviews submits collection work for connected sources. Check source totals as the results arrive.
e: Google reviews stop syncing to MoM even though the listing has newer reviews
A retry imports a previously collected review again

NODES.d: Compare a recent provider review with Web Dash and MoM. The scrum team reports that reconnecting Google is a workaround for PROD 5032.
e: Reconnect selects another listing with a similar name
Gap is hidden by unrelated reviews
Only the displayed total is checked after reconnecting

NODES.d: Filter by source, rating or reply and read status. Open a matching review and inspect its content. The dashboard saves the chosen reporting duration locally. Check the period again after moving between restaurants.
e: Read and replied filters are confused
A retained source filter hides recent feedback

NODES.d: Check the source, date, rating and text. Order or ticket context is available where the review has an associated ticket.
e: Ticket context is displayed against the wrong review
Operator refers to another guest order
A provider review with no order link looks like an incomplete import

NODES.d: Reading status and published response status are separate measures in Review Management.
e: Marking read removes the review from an unread queue before anyone replies
Mobile and dashboard read counts diverge

NODES.d: Google and Yelp have reply integrations. For other sources verify the available action before composing a public response.
e: Unsupported source offers a reply action that fails at submit
A reply action is unavailable for a supported review
Complaint cannot be answered from the inbox

NODES.d: Write a response or generate an AI suggestion for this review and edit the proposed wording before sending.
e: Draft cites an item or refund absent from the review
Restaurant makes an incorrect public promise
An earlier suggestion remains when the operator opens another review

NODES.d: AIO forwards the response to Google or Yelp and stores the result locally. Existing replies can restrict a second submission depending on source.
e: Provider accepts the reply but local saving fails
Two managers reply to the same review from different devices

NODES.d: Check that the response visible on the source matches the restaurant, review and intended text.
e: A local success message appears while the public reply is absent
Guest believes the complaint was ignored
Public reply contains personal order details from the inbox

NODES.d: The removal service calls Google and marks the saved reply deleted after success. Provider support varies.
e: Google removes the reply but the inbox still shows replied
Staff cannot tell whether to respond again
Operator expects the same removal option on another source

NODES.d: Request analysis of available reviews. The service distinguishes an in-progress run from insufficient data and handles completion separately.
e: Insufficient reviews leave the page waiting for a completion signal
An older summary appears while a new analysis is in progress

NODES.d: Inspect sentiments, keywords, categories and suggestions. Compare a theme to the underlying reviews and date range.
e: A repeated review dominates a small sample
Priority is set from duplicate feedback
A filtered inbox is compared with restaurant-wide insights

NODES.d: Compare MoM unread and negative counts with the same restaurant and source reviews in Web Dash.
e: Mobile summary stays stale after the web inbox updates
Unread is interpreted as negative feedback

NODES.d: Use the source connection controls and confirm the intended restaurant before disconnecting.
e: Disconnecting the wrong Google listing interrupts collection
New reviews disappear from the inbox
Old reviews still on screen imply that collection continues

NODES.d: Compare the latest review, reply or connection state on the intended surface.
e: Checking only a total hides a missing or duplicated individual review

NODES.d: The restaurant weekly summary is scheduled and handed to the notification service for delivery. Compare the period and restaurant with the inbox, and check the recorded outcome separately from receipt.
e: Report is sent to an outdated distribution list after a management change
Delivery succeeds but its saved status fails to update
The same report may be sent again

NODES.d: The service produces a restaurant-specific Excel export containing review and analysis data. Confirm that the requesting role has the appropriate route to use it.
e: An export is compared with a filtered inbox while the file contains a broader set
A download stops partway through and appears complete

PATHS.n: Start with a single provider and confirm feedback in both views.

PATHS.s: A1 A2 A3 A5 A3 A5 B2 C1 E5

PATHS.n: Compare an identifiable review, reconnect and check the mobile summary.
PATHS.s: A1 B2 B3 A2 A5 B2 E3 E5

PATHS.n: Read a Google or Yelp review and verify the public reply.
PATHS.s: A1 C1 C2 C3 C4 D1 D2 D3 E5

PATHS.n: Verify the existing reply, remove it and send a corrected response.
PATHS.s: A1 C1 C2 D4 D1 D2 D3 E5

PATHS.n: Collect a review and check what action the provider supports.
PATHS.s: A1 A4 A5 B1 B2 C1 C2 C4 E5

PATHS.n: Generate insights from available feedback and compare with source reviews.
PATHS.s: A1 E1 E2 C1 C2 E5

PATHS.n: Review the listing and confirm the change in connection state.
Check the report period, supporting reviews and restaurant export.
PATHS.s: A1 E6 E2 C1 E7 E5

NOTES: PROD 5032 records the MoM sync symptom. Reconnecting Google is a reported workaround. The production root cause is open.

The first fetch and insight status transitions are visible in Zeus. Provider collection cadence, exact analysis refresh time, mobile screens and notification delivery require operational verification.
Google and Yelp have outbound reply handlers. Google has a deletion handler. Tripadvisor reply publication was not found in the same path.
Weekly email scheduling and restaurant export are present. Confirm the actual recipients, delivery and mobile display with the restaurant.
